A1.justification: Both complete 35-page PDFs describe SaFa and support comparison of the text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original audio and panorama generation experiments, Fourier analyses, ablations, length-adaptation tests and user studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and expands the reported Fourier analysis across denoising steps.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the reference-guidance condition from t >= rguide*T to t >= (1-rguide)*T. This corrects the pseudocode to match the early guidance already described in v1, without establishing an implementation change. Both swap operators and the Make-An-Audio2-specific SaFa+ adaptations remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use AudioCaps and the same soundscape, sound-effect, music and panorama coverage. Longer-audio and wider-panorama tests already appear in v1's appendices; the broader v2 title does not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MD, MD*, MAD and, for panoramas, SyncDiffusion. AudioGen, Stable Diffusion Audio and Make-An-Audio2 remain the training-based comparators. The checkpoint comparison moves from v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 6 without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: v1 Section 3.1 gives a shared 10-second-segment setup; v2 Section 4.1 specifies 8-second segments for qualitative evaluation while retaining 10-second quantitative segments. Panorama FID/KID cropping is described using five equal regions instead of general sliding-window cropping. These reported protocol refinements do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 2 expands the averaging-versus-swap Fourier analysis to curves at denoising steps 2, 68, 134 and 200. Existing guidance-rate, swap-interval, component-ablation, checkpoint-failure and length-adaptation analyses are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Empirical uncertainty reporting remains unchanged: neither version supplies seed-level variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. User-study participation remains 39 recruited and 34 valid responses. The new probabilistic bound is theoretical, not experimental uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Most quantitative scores and user-study results match. Panorama runtimes change in v1 Table 3 versus v2 Table 4, including SD 2.0 SaFa from 35.16 to 19.15 seconds and SD 3.5 MD from 63.84 to 103.85 seconds. SD 2.0 SaFa* I-LPIPS changes from 0.62 to 0.65. These are revised reported values, not established algorithmic speed gains.

T1.justification: Beyond the existing method equations, v2 adds Appendix 8: a bounded-score assumption, reverse VP-SDE formulation, proposition with a high-probability distance bound, proof and reference-guided-swap corollary. Equations 12–17 introduce substantial formal analysis absent from v1.

C1.justification: The central two-swap and cross-modality contributions remain. The explicit efficiency claim changes from 11–14 times faster than SyncDiffusion in v1 to 2–20 times faster than MAD/SyncDiffusion in v2. The abstract also newly emphasizes retained length-adaptation results.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations connecting VAE connectivity to local convolutional correspondence and row-wise swapping to neighboring-token correlations in attention. Appendix 8 interprets its proposed bound as explaining similarity-diversity control. Existing over-guidance failure conditions and limitations concerning 1D or discrete representations remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies HiFi-GAN as the vocoder and explains extending open-source Stable Audio through initial-noise sizing. Conversely, it omits v1's named PANNs/VGGish metric backbones and MAD's explicit first-60-of-200-steps schedule. The project-page access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive positioning against ScaleCrafter and DemoFusion and references PanoFree and omni-aware outpainting. It removes extended latent-representation background and the SDEdit analogy. The central positioning against MD, MAD and SyncDiffusion remains.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and methodological explanations, moves condensed related work before methodology, and reorganizes the experimental appendices. Duplicated latent-diffusion background is removed, while the title, terminology, author ordering and section structure also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds a front-page composite, substantially redraws Figures 2–3, annotates qualitative failures and moves the audio length-adaptation table into the main text. The guidance sweep and 20-page qualitative gallery are retained. Document layout and table presentation also change extensively.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the diagrams and organization and corrects Algorithm 1. However, its new theoretical guarantee is not established by the supplied proof: Equations 15–16 omit squared-norm cross terms without justification. Most empirical evidence remains unchanged, and some reproducibility details disappear. These clarity gains and reliability losses prevent a confident judgment of net improvement.
